## Perito Moreno ice trekking: walk on a real glacier

You can see [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/) from purpose-built viewing walkways, from the water, or on a guided walk on the ice itself. Ice trekking is all about that third experience: stepping onto the glacier's surface and seeing its crevasses, blue ridges, and extraordinary contours up close. Preparing for such a day is quite different from preparing for a trip focused on panoramic photographs.

Our excursion includes **a walk on the glacier and a cocktail served with ice taken from the glacier**. This excursion is listed as an optional extra and is paid for separately. Age eligibility, the exact length of the walk, the guide's language, transfers, and the equipment provided all need to be confirmed. These conditions should be checked for your specific date before payment.

## How walking on the ice differs from the viewpoints

On the walkways in [Los Glaciares National Park](/argentina/place/los-glaciares-national-park/), visitors view the tall ice front from the shore. You can move between viewpoints, choose how far to walk, and photograph the glacier from different elevations. The panorama is the focus of most of the visit.

During an ice trek, the glacier's surface takes center stage. The national park administration describes such walks as guided outings using special crampons, led by trained guides. Visitors must not leave the permitted route independently or approach dangerous crevasses. The operator determines the exact route, technical equipment, and acceptable level of exertion; these cannot be inferred from general descriptions of the glacier.

For a first visit to Patagonia without a sporting activity, the [full-day bus excursion to Perito Moreno](/argentina/el-calafate/perito-moreno-full-day-bus/) is a suitable option. It includes viewing platforms and a return to [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/), but does not include a confirmed walk on the ice. If you book both experiences, it helps to understand how they differ.

## Preparation and participation restrictions

The glacier's surface is uneven, and walking on it requires close attention to your guide's instructions. Before booking, find out the permitted age range, fitness and health requirements, the length of the walk on ice, travel time, and weather-related cancellation rules. A lack of mountaineering experience does not automatically qualify or disqualify you; eligibility depends on the specific type of ice trek.

Weather in Argentine Patagonia is changeable. Strong winds, precipitation, and falling temperatures may affect the route and time at the glacier. Allow a buffer between the end of the excursion and international flight connections. If ice trekking is central to your trip, discuss whether the itinerary days can be rearranged in case of weather restrictions.

Dress in layers: a warm mid-layer, a windproof and waterproof jacket, gloves, and appropriate footwear. Request the specialist equipment list from the operator rather than assuming crampons, special boots, or any other items are included in this particular excursion. Also check whether you need insurance covering this activity.

## Choosing between the ice, a boat, and the shore

| Experience | Main attraction |
|---|---|
| Ice trekking | Walking on the glacier |
| Bus excursion | Views from the platforms |
| Boat trip near the glacier | Seeing the ice wall from the water |

A [private excursion to Perito Moreno](/argentina/el-calafate/argentina-perito-moreno-private-full-day/) offers a different way to organize the day and the guiding, but a private format does not automatically make it an ice trek. The [boat safari excursion](/argentina/perito-moreno-glacier/perito-moreno-boat-safari-russian-guide/) focuses on viewing the glacier from the water. To discover other glaciers on Lake Argentino, there is also the [Todo Glaciares navigation](/argentina/el-calafate/todo-glaciares/).

Choose according to what you want to do, rather than only the photographs of the ice wall. Some travelers are happy with the panorama from land; for others, the opportunity to walk on the ice is worth the additional preparation.

## Frequently asked questions about Perito Moreno ice trekking

### Can I walk onto the glacier independently?

No. Tourist walks on the ice take place in permitted areas, with specialized supervision and equipment, according to the operator's rules.

### Is ice trekking included in a regular visit to the glacier?

No. With Ada Tours, this is a separate optional excursion. The [bus excursion with viewing platforms](/argentina/el-calafate/perito-moreno-full-day-bus/) follows a different itinerary.

### How long does the walk on the ice take?

The exact duration must be confirmed separately. Ask for both the time spent actually walking on the ice and the total length of the outing from El Calafate.

### Are transfers, special boots, and the park entrance ticket included?

These services must be agreed separately. The glacier walk and cocktail with glacier ice are confirmed; the remaining inclusions depend on the selected offer.

## Which tours include the option of Perito Moreno ice trekking?

[Perito Moreno ice trekking](/argentina/el-calafate/perito-moreno-glacier-ice-trekking/) is a guided walk on the surface of [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/). Unlike a regular excursion to the viewing walkways, it requires suitable physical fitness and specialist equipment.

On our itineraries, this activity is linked to visits to the glacier from [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/). However, **the appearance of ice trekking in a tour's excursion list does not mean it is included in the base price**. Several current itineraries explicitly offer it as a paid extra.

## Itineraries offering an additional walk on the glacier

| Journey | Ice trekking conditions |
|---|---|
| [Brazil, Peru, Argentina — 15 days](/multi-country/tour/brazil-peru-argentina-group-15-days/) | Day 12, additional $300 |
| [Best of Argentina — 14 days](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-14-days/) | Day 5, additional $500 |

On the [15-day group itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-peru-argentina-group-15-days/), the glacier visit falls during the Argentine leg, after Brazil and Peru. The standard bus excursion to Perito Moreno is included, while ice trekking is offered as an optional activity.

On the [14-day Best of Argentina tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-14-days/), day five is devoted to the glacier. The main visit is from the shore, in a group with an English-speaking guide. Ice trekking can be added for an extra charge; the following day is devoted to traveling to Ushuaia.

These amounts apply to the specific published itineraries. **Do not treat them as a universal price** for every date and every version of the excursion. Check the conditions of your chosen trip before booking.

## What you can see on the ice and without trekking

In [Los Glaciares National Park](/argentina/place/los-glaciares-national-park/), there are several ways to experience Perito Moreno. On the shore, visitors stop at viewing platforms and look at the ice wall from different elevations. This is part of the regular [bus excursion](/argentina/el-calafate/perito-moreno-full-day-bus/).

On an ice trek, the group steps directly onto the glacier. Organized walks use crampons attached to footwear, and participants follow trained guides. The surface is uneven, with crevasses and wet patches; the route and walking distance depend on the particular trek and its safety requirements.

The description of Ada Tours' separate excursion module mentions a cocktail served with ice taken from the glacier. This is one feature of the experience, but it does not replace eligibility checks or mean every trip to Perito Moreno includes walking on the ice.

If you would rather admire and photograph the glacier from viewing platforms without specialist equipment, [tours with a bus excursion](/argentina/el-calafate/perito-moreno-full-day-bus/tour/) are the better fit. To observe several glaciers from the water, consider the separate [Todo Glaciares navigation](/argentina/el-calafate/todo-glaciares/).

## How to choose a multi-day itinerary

Begin with the geography of the whole trip. Some travelers want to concentrate on one Argentine region; others hope to visit Buenos Aires, Ushuaia, Bariloche, Iguazú, or neighboring countries as well. Ice trekking should fit into this sequence without turning the day before a flight into a race against time.

Then check four things:

1. **Payment.** What is included in the main Perito Moreno day, and how much does the ice trek cost separately?
2. **Eligibility.** Is the specific walk suitable given participants' ages, health, fitness, and any restrictions?
3. **Time.** Is there enough time for the briefing, travel to the starting point, and the trek itself?
4. **Equipment.** Who supplies crampons and other required gear, and what footwear and clothing must travelers bring?

We can help arrange the excursion days in a suitable order and clarify the operator's current conditions. Eligibility for the ice route depends on the selected product's rules, while availability also depends on weather and ice conditions.

## What to bring and how to assess the physical effort

Even in summer, Patagonia's weather changes quickly. Bring warm layers, protection from wind and rain, comfortable shoes, and sunglasses. Obtain the exact footwear and fitness requirements for your chosen ice trek in advance.

You must not leave the permitted route independently or approach crevasses. Argentina's national park administration recommends staying on marked paths and following accompanying guides' instructions. In challenging weather, whether the ice excursion goes ahead depends on the actual safety of the route.

A regular walk on the viewing platforms is much less demanding, although there may still be stairs and changes in elevation. If your group has different physical abilities, discuss in advance who will be comfortable on a sightseeing excursion and who may prefer the separate trek.

## Frequently asked questions about tours with Perito Moreno ice trekking

### Is ice trekking included in every tour featuring Perito Moreno?

No. On the itineraries named above, it is a separately paid optional excursion. The included visit to the viewing platforms and the walk on the ice have different pricing and arrangements.

### Where does the trip start?

[El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/) is the base. The precise ice trek starting point and included transfers depend on the specific excursion.

### Do I need mountaineering experience?

Some organized formats do not require mountaineering experience, but fitness, age, and equipment requirements still apply. Check these for the actual product, rather than judging by the general word "trekking."

### Can I visit the glacier without walking on the ice?

Yes. A regular visit to the viewing platforms is a separate part of several tours. [Ice trekking](/argentina/el-calafate/perito-moreno-glacier-ice-trekking/) remains an optional extra.

## Perito Moreno Glacier with a Russian-speaking guide: an excursion from El Calafate

[Perito Moreno](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/) is one of Argentine Patagonia's major natural attractions. The ice front towers above the lake, and the walkways and viewpoints reveal deep crevasses and blue ridges of ice. For travelers who prefer to learn about the region's history and nature in Russian, Ada Tours offers a separate excursion with a **Russian-speaking guide**.

The excursion costs **$188 per person**. A **discount may be available for 2 or more participants**, although the amount is not specified. The duration, exact transport arrangements, and any other included services must be confirmed separately; conditions from other excursions to the same glacier do not automatically apply.

## Where Perito Moreno is and how to visit

The starting area is [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/) and Los Glaciares National Park. Perito Moreno is a glacier descending toward Lake Argentino, forming a wall of ice along the water. It is within **Los Glaciares National Park**, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It should not be confused with the separate Perito Moreno National Park in another part of Patagonia.

A typical visit takes place on specially constructed walkways and viewing platforms. You can choose different elevations and viewing angles, see the folds of the ice front, and appreciate the scale of the glacier without setting foot on the ice. The exact platforms used and the amount of time spent at them are not specified for this offer.

The experience changes with the weather: sunlight alters the hues of the ice, while rain and wind make walking on exposed platforms more difficult. Choosing a date solely in the hope of "perfect weather" is difficult, so layered clothing and rain protection are useful.

## What a Russian-speaking guide adds

Your guide explains how glaciers form, how their fronts change, and why large blocks of ice sometimes break away. However, **it is impossible to guarantee that a calving event will occur at a particular time**. The vast ice wall and surrounding mountains are impressive even without one.

Russian-language guiding is particularly convenient if you want to ask questions freely about Patagonia's natural environment, visiting conditions, and the history of the protected area. This format does not mean park admission, lunch, or transport are necessarily included: these items are not separately listed among the currently structured inclusions.

## How it differs from the English-speaking guide option

You can also choose the [six-hour excursion with an English-speaking guide](/argentina/el-calafate/perito-moreno-english-speaking-guide/) for $165. This option explicitly includes a private transfer and excludes lunch. The Russian-language version has different stated conditions: the guiding language, a price of $188 per person, and the possibility of a discount for groups of at least 2.

| Condition | Russian-speaking guide | English-speaking guide |
|---|---|---|
| Listed price | $188/person | $165 |
| Duration | Not specified | 6 hours |
| Transfer | Not confirmed | Private transfer included |
| Meals | Not confirmed | Lunch not included |

The prices have **different bases**: the Russian-language option explicitly states a per-person price, whereas the unit for the $165 English-language rate is not specified. This is not a ready-made comparison of savings on identical terms. Compare the total cost for your group and the complete list of included services.

## Do you need a boat trip or a walk on the glacier?

The glacier is already clearly visible from the shore, but other formats are also available: [specialist ice trekking](/argentina/el-calafate/perito-moreno-glacier-ice-trekking/), a [full-day bus excursion](/argentina/el-calafate/perito-moreno-full-day-bus/), or a [program combining viewpoints with a boat safari](/argentina/perito-moreno-glacier/perito-moreno-boat-safari-russian-guide/).

**Neither a boat trip nor a guided walk on the ice with crampons is specified** for the excursion described here. Those activities have their own conditions and fitness or health restrictions. Do not add them simply because they are available in the region.

## Preparing for the visit

When traveling from El Calafate, allow time for the drive to the park and for walking on the viewing platforms. Patagonia can be very windy; closed, non-slip shoes, a windproof outer layer, and rain protection will be useful. Signs and railings at the viewpoints help prevent falls on slippery surfaces.

When booking, confirm the departure point, duration, park admission, car transfers, lunch, and whether the walk can be adapted for limited mobility. These are points to clarify when agreeing on the service, not additional promises about what the tour includes.

[Nature-focused trips in Argentina](/interests/wildlife/tours/argentina/) let you combine glaciers with other regions. When choosing a multi-day tour, check which days and destinations are allocated time.

## Frequently asked questions about Perito Moreno with a Russian-speaking guide

### How much does the excursion cost?

The price is **$188 per person**. A discount may be available for groups of 2 or more, with the amount determined when the arrangements are agreed.

### How many hours does it last?

The fixed duration of this version is confirmed at booking. The travel time, stops, and return need to be agreed.

### Is the national park entrance ticket included?

Park admission must be confirmed separately, along with transport and meals.

### Do I need to go out onto the glacier?

There are viewing walkways for experiencing Perito Moreno. Walking on the ice is a separate specialist activity and is not specifically offered as part of this excursion.

### Can I expect to see ice breaking off the glacier?

Ice calving is a natural process without a fixed schedule. It cannot be promised on any particular excursion.

## Todo Glaciares: several glaciers in one day

**Todo Glaciares** is for travelers who want to explore Patagonia's glaciers from the water and devote a full day to the experience. Departure is from Punta Bandera port, about 47 km from [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/). The vessel travels through the northern part of [Lake Argentino](/argentina/place/lake-argentino/), where one glacier follows another and icebergs can be seen floating in the channels.

Unlike a short boat outing near a single glacier, this is an extended route with a stop ashore. Our main destinations are **Upsala and Spegazzini**. The itinerary also mentions the Seco, Heim Sur, and Peineta glaciers, which can be seen along the way.

## The route from Punta Bandera to Spegazzini

First, the boat crosses a section of the lake known as Boca del Diablo and heads toward the Upsala Channel. Large icebergs that have broken from the glacier's front may be seen nearby. Their shapes, numbers, and locations vary, and how closely the boat can approach depends on conditions on the water. Excellent photographs are possible even away from the ice wall itself: icebergs, mountains, and dark water create striking scenes.

The route then continues into the Spegazzini Channel. On this stretch, you can see the Seco, Spegazzini, Heim Sur, and Peineta glaciers. This is an opportunity to compare different glacier fronts on one journey: some descend into the water, while others are visible higher up the slopes.

After the boat portion, there is **a landing at Spegazzini Base**. Here, you walk about 300 m along a forest trail toward the refuge, viewing platforms, and interpretive stops. It is a short walk on land, not a climb or a trek over the glacier's surface.

## What you see from the boat and from the shore

From the vessel, the main attractions are the glaciers and the geography of [Lake Argentino](/argentina/place/lake-argentino/): its arms, channels, shores, and icebergs. The stop on land offers a different perspective. Viewpoints reveal the surrounding terrain, while the forest walk adds variety to the day.

Los Glaciares National Park officially lists Todo Glaciares among the boat navigations departing from Punta Bandera. The park also describes the refuge at Spegazzini, with viewing paths and visitor facilities. The existence of these facilities **does not mean** that meals, drinks, or other purchases are included in the Ada Tours offer. Of the services mentioned here, only the transfer back to the hotel after the return is confirmed.

For viewing the glaciers from land-based walkways, a separate excursion to [Perito Moreno](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/) is more suitable. Todo Glaciares primarily explores the northern arms of the lake.

## Price and planning from El Calafate

The excursion starts **from $336** and lasts **a full day**. After returning to Punta Bandera, a transfer to your hotel is provided. Transport **to the port**, national park admission, and meals have not been confirmed among the included services, so clarify them separately when arranging the excursion.

Leave some extra time on the navigation day and avoid a tight connection immediately after your return. Weather in this part of Patagonia changes quickly: wind, visibility, water conditions, and the concentration of ice may affect the vessel's passage. The precise order of stops depends on the scheduled departure and the crew's decisions.

Dress carefully, even in summer. A windproof outer layer, warm sweater, shoes with reliable soles, and protection for your belongings against spray will make the boat trip more comfortable. Closed footwear is generally better for the short trail at Spegazzini Base than light city shoes.

## Differences from Glaciares Gourmet and ice trekking

[Glaciares Gourmet](/argentina/el-calafate/glaciares-gourmet/) is also a full-day navigation on the lake, but with a different arrangement: the Maria Turquesa yacht, a stop at Puesto de Las Vacas, a stated visit to Perito Moreno, and a choice of meals including a Premium option for an additional charge. Todo Glaciares focuses on **Upsala, Spegazzini, and the landing at Spegazzini Base**.

If you want to walk on the ice instead of looking at a glacier from a boat, consider the [Perito Moreno ice trekking excursion](/argentina/el-calafate/perito-moreno-glacier-ice-trekking/). Its physical requirements and organization differ from those of Todo Glaciares.

| Travel goal | Option to consider |
|---|---|
| Upsala and Spegazzini | Todo Glaciares |
| Yacht and gastronomic experience | Glaciares Gourmet |
| Walking on the ice | Ice trekking |

The precise content of each excursion matters more than the similarities between glacier photographs. When planning a trip through [Argentina](/argentina/), Ada Tours can help choose an option that fits your time in El Calafate.

## Frequently asked questions about Todo Glaciares

### Does Todo Glaciares visit Perito Moreno Glacier?

The main destinations on this itinerary are Upsala and Spegazzini, as well as glaciers in the lake's northern channels. **A stop at Perito Moreno is not confirmed for Todo Glaciares**. It is included in the separate [Glaciares Gourmet navigation](/argentina/el-calafate/glaciares-gourmet/).

### Do I have to walk on a glacier?

No. Todo Glaciares includes a walk of about 300 m on a forest path at Spegazzini Base. This takes place on land. Walking on the glacier's surface is a separate activity.

### How long does the excursion take?

It is a **full-day** trip from the El Calafate area. On departure day, allow time to reach Punta Bandera, board the vessel, complete the navigation, and return to town.

### Are meals included in the Todo Glaciares price?

Meals have not been confirmed among the included services. Before booking, clarify meal arrangements, entrance fees, and transport to the departure port.

## Tours offering Todo Glaciares navigation on Lake Argentino

[Todo Glaciares](/argentina/el-calafate/todo-glaciares/) is a full-day boat navigation on [Lake Argentino](/argentina/place/lake-argentino/) in [Los Glaciares National Park](/argentina/place/los-glaciares-national-park/). Its main sights are the Upsala and Spegazzini glaciers, icebergs in the northern arms of the lake, and a landing at Spegazzini Base.

On two of our itineraries, this trip is available **on a free day in El Calafate**, after the main visit to Perito Moreno. This is an essential distinction: the possibility of adding an excursion does not mean that it is included in the price of the multi-day journey.

## Which itineraries offer Todo Glaciares?

| Tour | Day available for optional navigation |
|---|---|
| [Incredible Argentina — 13 days](/multi-country/tour/incredible-argentina-patagonia/) | Day 8, free day |
| [Highlights of Argentina — 16 days](/argentina/tour/explore-argentina-16-days/) | Day 11, free day |

On the [13-day Incredible Argentina itinerary](/multi-country/tour/incredible-argentina-patagonia/), travelers visit Buenos Aires, Ushuaia, El Calafate, and Iguazú. On day seven, they see Perito Moreno from the viewpoints and take a separate boat safari in Rico Bay. Day eight can be spent independently or used for an optional navigation, including Todo Glaciares or Glaciares Gourmet.

On the [16-day Highlights of Argentina journey](/argentina/tour/explore-argentina-16-days/), the preceding day ten is also devoted to Perito Moreno and a short boat excursion near the ice front. Day eleven is free for a choice of optional excursions, including Todo Glaciares. On the next day, the trip continues with a flight via Buenos Aires to Iguazú.

This order lets travelers see Perito Moreno itself from the shore and, if they wish, devote another whole day to other glaciers. Choose the tour based on its complete program, duration, and the time available in Patagonia.

## Why Todo Glaciares is different from the Perito Moreno boat safari

These are two different kinds of navigation.

**The Perito Moreno boat safari** complements a shore excursion to a single glacier. The boat travels through Rico Bay, approaches the ice front, and offers views of the glacier from the lake. Such a boat excursion is included in the main glacier days of both multi-day itineraries.

**Todo Glaciares** covers the northern part of Lake Argentino. From Punta Bandera, the vessel passes Boca del Diablo and Upsala Channel, then heads toward Spegazzini Channel. Along the route, passengers see icebergs and several glacier areas; the canonical excursion description also names Seco, Heim Sur, and Peineta. A landing at Spegazzini Base is included.

These experiences therefore complement each other if you want to see different glaciers rather than just the same ice front from two sides. Todo Glaciares does not replace walking on [Perito Moreno's viewing platforms](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/), and it is not an ice trek.

## What a day on the water looks like

The basic route begins at Punta Bandera, about 47 km from [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/). The boat travels across the lake between mountain shores, with changing views of ice walls and icebergs along the way.

At Spegazzini Base, the group lands and walks about 300 meters along a forest trail to the refuge and viewing platforms. Although this is a short walk, comfortable shoes and wind protection are useful. Most of the day is spent on the boat, so travelers prone to seasickness should discuss the sailing conditions in advance.

The separate [Todo Glaciares excursion](/argentina/el-calafate/todo-glaciares/) provides a return transfer to the hotel after the navigation. However, this does not automatically mean every version includes the drive to the port, meals, and all other services. Check the exact inclusions for the selected tour and excursion.

Ice conditions and weather can change the vessel's route and the distance from which glaciers are viewed. A close approach to each glacier is not guaranteed regardless of sailing conditions.

## How to choose an optional excursion

If you only want to see Perito Moreno, both tours already have a dedicated day for it. Todo Glaciares is worth adding when you want to see Upsala and Spegazzini, spend more time on the water, and experience the northern glacier areas of the park.

Before selecting the navigation, clarify the services included, transport to Punta Bandera, time spent ashore, possible weather-related changes, and cancellation rules. The separate excursion in the Ada Tours catalog starts from $336; this is its own starting price, **not part of the multi-day tour's base fare**.

To compare other formats, see [Perito Moreno ice trekking](/argentina/el-calafate/perito-moreno-glacier-ice-trekking/) and [tours with a bus excursion to the glacier](/argentina/el-calafate/perito-moreno-full-day-bus/tour/). A wider choice is available in the [tour catalog for El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about Todo Glaciares on multi-day tours

### Is Todo Glaciares included in the price of Incredible Argentina?

There is no basis for treating it as included: on the [13-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/incredible-argentina-patagonia/), navigation is listed as an optional excursion for the free eighth day. It is arranged separately.

### When can I choose Todo Glaciares on the 16-day itinerary?

On day eleven, which is left free in El Calafate. Day ten is devoted to Perito Moreno, and day twelve involves the onward flight.

### Will we visit Perito Moreno itself during Todo Glaciares?

The main Todo Glaciares route heads toward the Upsala and Spegazzini glaciers. On the tours discussed here, Perito Moreno is visited on a separate day.

### Do I need to know how to walk on a glacier?

No. Todo Glaciares is a boat excursion with a brief walk ashore. Walking on the ice in crampons belongs to a [different excursion format](/argentina/el-calafate/perito-moreno-glacier-ice-trekking/).
